agree.reason: The cash cliff and the honest break-even math make a credible case, but a partner who thinks sales are slow gets no plan for selling faster and no monthly cash report, so they may wait rather than commit.

honest.reason: Nothing is invented and profit is not promised, but the $103 first-year figure is revenue and sits under a 'margin' heading, which makes the unit economics look better than they are.

works_the_facts.reason: Good derived figures (520 colonies saved, $17 to $7 margin at $45, under $30,000 by March, runway to about October 2027, break-even needing revenue to more than double against 2.6x customer growth), though break-even compares revenue with total spending and ignores cost of goods.

right_comparison.reason: Not raising is shown concretely: under half a month of cash just as the revenue season starts, set against last year's growth trend.

qualification.reason: The profit hedge gives a checkable window (March and April) and a consequence, but it states no revenue threshold for that spring and drops the committed monthly cash report that would let investors check it.

objections.reason: The slow-sales worry gets only the 12-to-31 growth figure, and the note raises three customers testing the competitor and an undecided price without answering what HiveSense will do about either.

fit.reason: Right form and under 600 words, but it asks for replies by the December 15 close instead of the December 1 deadline the founder gave.
